- name: Conformance sweep (world scope)
        # The tree as it stands, the pattern bootstrap wires into consumers.
        run: node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      - name: Conformance sweep (work scope)
        # The CHANGE, not the tree: this branch's diff against origin/main, which
        # is the only scope that can see what a commit did rather than what the
        # repo now contains. It used to run at the session's Stop hook and nowhere
        # else, so a rule about the change was enforced only where a session
        # happened to be — a hand-pushed branch, an interrupted session, or a hook
        # that never fired reached main unjudged.
        #
        # Base ref explicitly: actions/checkout leaves no origin/main behind, and
        # a work scope with no base resolves to an empty diff — which passes every
        # rule silently. Fetching it first is what keeps a green run meaningful.
        #
        # No --transcript, so the conversation-surface rules (comment-classification)
        # self-skip; every file- and commit-scoped work rule runs.
        #
        # NOT ON claudinite/* — the automation's own delivery branches: the update
        # and maintenance PRs, and every deliverGenerated artifact. None has a
        # session or an issue behind it, so task-lifecycle would red a nightly
        # regenerate for lacking a task it never had. Their gate is the world sweep
        # and the self-test. A push to main is skipped for the same reason it is
        # meaningless: the branch IS the base, so the diff is empty by construction.

input.body:
Refs #939. Follows [#965](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/965), which added `pack-version-bumped` — a work-scope rule, and therefore one that until now ran only where a session ran.

CI swept the **world** (the tree as it stands) and nothing swept the **work** (what this change did). So every commit-scoped rule — `task-lifecycle`, `squash-merge-history`, `consumer-safe-change`, `pack-version-bumped` — was enforced by the Stop hook or not at all: a hand-pushed branch, an interrupted session, or a hook that never fired reached `main` unjudged.

**The step.** `check_the_work.mjs --changed --base origin/main`, after an explicit fetch of that ref. Both halves matter: `actions/checkout` leaves no `origin/main` behind, and a work scope with **no base resolves to an empty diff** — which passes every rule, silently. That is the same shape of green-looking nothing #939 was made of, so `engine-tests/ci-work-scope.test.mjs` holds the step to running the runner, naming the base, and fetching it. Seen failing on both halves before it passed.

No `--transcript`, so the conversation-surface rules (`comment-classification`) self-skip; every file- and commit-scoped work rule runs.

**Not on `claudinite/*`.** The automation's own delivery branches — the update and maintenance PRs, and every `deliverGenerated` artifact (`claudinite/usage-fold`, `claudinite/fleet-usage`, `claudinite/fleet-digest-*`). None has a session or an issue behind it, so `task-lifecycle` would red a nightly regenerate for lacking a task it never had; their gate stays the world sweep and the self-test. A `push` to `main` is skipped for the reason it is meaningless there — the branch is the base.

**Verified end to end**, not just by the guard: a scratch branch editing `packs/basics/RULES.md` without a version bump, run through CI's exact invocation, exits 1 on `pack-version-bumped` (and on `task-lifecycle` for the deliberately issue-less probe commit). The real tree in that same invocation is clean. Full suite green (2078).

Not touched: the member-facing side. Consumers ship no CI workflow of their own and their maintenance PRs are all `claudinite/*` automation, so nothing here changes what the fleet is asked to run — worth a separate decision if you want members' own CI to gate the work scope too.

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4

      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level
        # (`packs-tests/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs` and so on), so a test at an unlisted depth
        # was silently never run — which is exactly how vendoring/'s two files sat outside
        # CI. `**` removes depth from the question; what remains is the root list, and
        # engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the moment a tracked test lands
        # outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit; adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs-tests/             every canon pack's tests, mirroring packs/
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        #   docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/ the dispatch design's executable scenarios — the
        #                            simulator lives beside the spec it models, not in
        #                            engine/ (nothing ships it; it tests prose)
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob

Refs #939. Follows [#965](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/965), which added `pack-version-bumped` — a work-scope rule, and therefore one that until now ran only where a session ran.

CI swept the **world** (the tree as it stands) and nothing swept the **work** (what this change did). So every commit-scoped rule — `task-lifecycle`, `squash-merge-history`, `consumer-safe-change`, `pack-version-bumped` — was enforced by the Stop hook or not at all: a hand-pushed branch, an interrupted session, or a hook that never fired reached `main` unjudged.

**The step.** `check_the_work.mjs --changed --base origin/main`, after an explicit fetch of that ref. Both halves matter: `actions/checkout` leaves no `origin/main` behind, and a work scope with **no base resolves to an empty diff** — which passes every rule, silently.

**And silence is not success.** The runner prints nothing on a clean sweep *and* nothing on a sweep that judged an empty diff — the first CI run of this step was green with no output at all, which proves neither. So the step now prints its scope and fails on an empty one:

```
work scope: 2 changed file(s) vs origin/main
```

`engine-tests/ci-work-scope.test.mjs` holds all four halves — the runner runs, the base is named, the base is fetched, an empty scope errors. Seen failing before it passed.

No `--transcript`, so the conversation-surface rules (`comment-classification`) self-skip; every file- and commit-scoped work rule runs.

**Not on `claudinite/*`.** The automation's own delivery branches — the update and maintenance PRs, and every `deliverGenerated` artifact (`claudinite/usage-fold`, `claudinite/fleet-usage`, `claudinite/fleet-digest-*`). None has a session or an issue behind it, so `task-lifecycle` would red a nightly regenerate for lacking a task it never had; their gate stays the world sweep and the self-test. A `push` to `main` is skipped for the reason it is meaningless there — the branch is the base.

**Verified in the real runner, not only by the guard:** [run 32075305013](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32075305013) shows the step executing, reporting `work scope: 2 changed file(s)`, and sweeping clean. And a scratch branch editing `packs/basics/RULES.md` without a version bump, through CI's exact invocation, exits 1 on `pack-version-bumped`. Full suite green (2079).

Not touched: the member-facing side. Consumers ship no CI workflow of their own and their maintenance PRs are all `claudinite/*` automation, so nothing here changes what the fleet is asked to run — worth a separate decision if you want members' own CI to gate the work scope too.

**New: [#966](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/966) — CI now runs the work scope**

- Two things I found while proving it, both fixed rather than shipped:
  - The first green run printed *nothing* — the runner is as silent on a clean sweep as on one that judged nothing. The step now prints `work scope: N changed file(s) vs origin/main` and errors when N is 0. The real run confirms it: [run 32075305013](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32075305013).
  - Bot branches would have gone red: `deliverGenerated` commits ("Claudinite: fold skill-usage metrics") cite no issue, so `task-lifecycle` would fail every nightly regenerate. The step skips `claudinite/*` — automation branches with no session and no task behind them — and pushes to `main`, where the diff is empty by construction.
- [`engine-tests/ci-work-scope.test.mjs`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/pack-version-validation-0rrjfk/engine-tests/ci-work-scope.test.mjs) guards all four properties, seen failing first. End-to-end proof: a scratch branch editing `packs/basics/RULES.md` without a bump exits 1 on `pack-version-bumped` through CI's exact invocation.

CI green on the PR. Not touched: members' own CI — consumers ship no workflow and their maintenance PRs are all `claudinite/*` anyway, so extending this to the fleet is a separate call.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#966](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/966) awaits your LGTM; whether members' CI should gate the work scope too; and #939's candidates (1) atomic packs+engine delivery and (3) the delivery-gate backstop.
